notes: T677 (false Claude window cooldown) — test-first; the seeded arms were RED against the 2026-08-22 code (quoted in findings/T677-false-cooldown-context.json), then GREEN. THE DEFECT, live: `family_cooldown('.')` armed claude OFF until 2026-08-23T02:09:22Z from T653 — a DEEPSEEK lane still running (`ps` live, run record has no exit/end) whose log merely QUOTED the provider's limit template because its brief told it to read wall-canary-preregistration.md. ROOT CAUSE CHAIN (all four defects): (a) scan_terminal claimed to scan only the last 8 KiB but actually scanned the WHOLE log; (b) the quoted doc carries 'tokens: no reading' (a FAILURE_EVIDENCE_RX match) within 400 bytes of 'hit your session limit', so the quote looked like a terminal death; (c) scan_terminal HARDCODED family='claude' — attribution was by proximity, never from the run record's model field; (d) reset '<time>' did not parse → FALLBACK_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=6h armed, anchored to the LIVE log's moving mtime (fresh → within ARM_FRESHNESS) and re-derived on every dispatch → the lockout extended itself. It was the fourth instance of the T526/T601/T643 defect class; T625/T630 fixed the refusal classifier the same way (classify from the runner's own terminal record, treat worker output as untrusted) and T628 reintroduced the grep in the window watcher. THE FIX — the same architectural correction, applied here: (1) a cooldown arms ONLY from a terminal RUN RECORD of a lane of that family (T628 stamp provider_limit/provider_reset_epoch/provider_reset_text, or T629 killed_by=provider-limit); the worker log is NEVER read; (2) family comes from the death record's own model field; (3) a lane with no terminal record (no exit/end — still running) is not a death and arms nothing (liveness); (4) an unparseable/absent reset arms a SHORT death-anchored fallback — FALLBACK_COOLDOWN_SECONDS 6h→30min (WEIZIGO_WINDOW_FALLBACK_SECONDS), stable across re-derivations (no self-extension) — and the existing watch() nudge + one-lane probe re-checks the provider (verify-don't-assume; a fresh death re-arms). FALLBACK REASONING (brief item 3): the old 6h bound was uncheckable, so it was not conservative, just expensive — it anchored to a live log's moving mtime and locked the family out for hours past a same-day reopen (the 12:47Z outage reopened at 13:00Z; a 6h fallback would have idled the fleet until ~18:47Z). 30 min ≥ the observed death→reset gap (13 min), short enough that a same-day reopen costs ≤ ~30 min of idle, long enough not to burn probe lanes every few minutes against a genuinely-closed window; each cycle costs one cheap lane, and the bound is now CHECKED by the probe, not assumed. (5) THE RECORDED OVERRIDE (brief item 4): --override-window-cooldown=<reason> on bin/dispatch AND bin/subagent — reason REQUIRED, appended to untracked/fleet-window-overrides.jsonl (append-only audit), loud WARNING on stderr, dry-run records nothing (a dry-run is not a decision). D040 (T612 amend, acked): (1) the false cooldown is EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED — a claude-haiku probe lane (T676) launched at ~20:1xZ while dispatch refused claude until 02:06Z ran to completion exit 0 verified pass; (2) the guard existed ONLY in bin/dispatch — bin/subagent (which dispatch calls) had no check, so the guard was advisory, and the probe went around it via the underlying layer. DECISION, recorded per D040: ENFORCE at the real launch chokepoint — bin/subagent now runs the same family_cooldown gate (every lane launch, dispatch or hand), with the same recorded override; dispatch's gate stays as the earlier, richer-diagnostic one and its refusal text now says the guard is enforced at subagent too. Rationale: a guard whose strength depends on which entry point the caller knows about is a guard in name only, and 'a guard people route around teaches everyone to route around guards'; the T677 record-only arming removes the false-arm class that made enforcement risky. Both bin/subagent holders (T494, T552) are DONE; the one-writer hold was declared on the kanban (holds=[tools/window_policy.py, bin/subagent]) and cleared after commit. T628 RELATIONSHIP (the brief's bar): the guard's PURPOSE was sound — it prevented a doomed re-dispatch tonight and that was right — and its EVIDENCE SOURCE was wrong; this is a correction of one arm of T628's work, not an argument against having the guard. T628 never committed: its window_policy.py / regression / dispatch gate / keeper wiring sat uncommitted in the working tree, so this commit carries both the preserved T628 mechanisms (reset watcher, token meter, fan-out cap, probe) and the T677 correction. CONTROLS (tools/regression-window-resilience.sh, 16 arms, hermetic scratch; B1/E1 use the REAL kept t653/t617 logs and SKIP loudly on a fresh clone): A1 killed_by+reset-text parses to 13:00Z (RED on old code: 6h fallback); A2 T628 stamp authoritative; A3 nudge/probe state machine; A4 dispatch refusal, deepseek unaffected; A5 provider-limit death reopens as provider-outage (kept verbatim); B1 THE T677 CASE — live deepseek lane quoting the template → no claude cooldown, claude dispatch proceeds (RED on old code: 'REFUSED — family claude is in window cooldown until 2026-08-23T02:15:06Z (reset '?' from T653)'); B2 quote-log with no record → nothing (RED on old code: armed with a PARSED reset from the quoted prose); B3 empty → nothing, SPEND, dispatch proceeds; C1 near-exhausted meter refuses over-budget claude, deepseek unaffected; C2 watchdog-killed lane + quote log → no cooldown (RED on old code: armed ~16.7h from the log); C3 wall-killed lane → no cooldown (RED); C4 deepseek provider-limit death → no claude cooldown; D1 unparseable reset → death-anchored 1800s fallback, stable across re-derivation (RED on old code: 6h sliding); D2 override proceeds with reason + append-only record + bare flag refused; E1 subagent ENFORCES the cooldown (D040), override proceeds, deepseek unaffected. Wired into `zig build test` (build.zig). REMAINING SURFACE, stated honestly: tools/bakeoff.sh launches `tools/runner` directly (never bin/subagent) — bakeoff lanes bypass the cooldown gate; bakeoff is a deliberate, operator-launched experiment harness with its own isolation gates (--allow-unisolated), so this is documented as a known surface, not silently left. Also: the 2026-08-22 outage lanes (T615/616/617/621/622) have run records predating T629's vocabulary — no killed_by — so they arm nothing today (deliberate: the record is the only evidence, and those records carry no classification; they are also long past ARM_FRESHNESS).
